newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica to boost shareholder value.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica to boost shareholder value.

text.p: Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga said on Monday that the company would focus on increasing shareholder value now that it had been fully privatised.
"We want to be a more and more global, competitive, efficient and stable company and thus increase the yield to our shareholders," Villalonga told a news conference.
Villalonga said the slide in Telefonica shares in the days following the privatisation supported the belief that Telefonica was a long-term investment opportunity.
Last Tuesday alone, after the sale of the state's remaining 20.9 percent stake, Telefonica's shares fell by 110 pesetas or 3.3 percent.
Following the sale, Villalonga said the company now had 1.2 million shareholders.
In the medium term, Villalonga said the core shareholders would remain the same: BBV, La Caixa and Argentaria .
The state received a total of 607 billion pesetas from the sale.

Deputy Economy Secretary Fernando Diaz Moreno said on Monday in addition, the Treasury would receive 130 billion pesetas this year from taxes on the capital gains made on the sale by state holding company SEPPa, and a further 50 billion in 1998.
